name: fix_wrong_join_type
description: Fixes a reporting query that drops customers with zero orders due to an INNER JOIN
prompts: schema.sql defines `customers` and `orders` tables (do not change schema.sql). report.sql is meant to produce one row per customer showing their id, name, how many orders they've placed (order_count), and their total spend (total_amount), including customers who have never placed a single order (those should show order_count 0 and total_amount 0). Right now report.sql uses an INNER JOIN between customers and orders, which silently drops any customer who has zero orders from the report - a customer with no orders should still appear as a row. Fix report.sql (and only report.sql) so every customer appears in the results, with order_count and total_amount both 0 for anyone who has never ordered.

setup_files.report.sql:
SELECT c.id AS customer_id, c.name AS customer_name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) AS total_amount
FROM customers c
INNER JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY c.id;

test_setup_files.test_report.py:
import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
with open('schema.sql', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    conn.executescript(f.read())

conn.execute("INSERT INTO customers (id, name) VALUES (1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Bob'), (3, 'Carol')")
conn.execute('INSERT INTO orders (id, customer_id, amount) VALUES (1, 1, 9.99), (2, 1, 19.99), (3, 2, 5.00)')
conn.commit()
# Carol (id=3) has placed no orders and must still appear in the report.

with open('report.sql', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    query = f.read()

rows = conn.execute(query).fetchall()
by_id = {r[0]: r for r in rows}

assert len(rows) == 3, f'expected all 3 customers in the report, got {len(rows)}: {rows}'
assert 3 in by_id, f'customer with zero orders (Carol, id=3) is missing from the report: {rows}'

carol = by_id[3]
assert carol[2] == 0, f'expected Carols order_count to be 0, got {carol}'
assert float(carol[3] or 0) == 0.0, f'expected Carols total_amount to be 0, got {carol}'

alice = by_id[1]
assert alice[2] == 2, f'expected Alice to have 2 orders, got {alice}'
assert abs(float(alice[3]) - 29.98) < 1e-9, f'expected Alice total_amount 29.98, got {alice}'

bob = by_id[2]
assert bob[2] == 1, f'expected Bob to have 1 order, got {bob}'
assert abs(float(bob[3]) - 5.00) < 1e-9, f'expected Bob total_amount 5.00, got {bob}'

print('PASS')
